newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Swedish retail sales rose two pct in 1996 - HUI.
newsitem.headline: Swedish retail sales rose two pct in 1996 - HUI.

text.p: Swedish retail sales rose two percent in fixed prices in 1996, according to Swedish Retail and Wholesale Research Institute (HUI) on Thursday.
A decrease in value added tax in January 1996 was a key contributor to this but despite this profitability did not rise, HUI told a press conference.
Increased staff costs were a big reason that profitability fell. The biggest rise was in daily goods which HUI estimated had risen three percent.
"It is alarming that profitability is getting worse and that it is particularly the small retail traders that are affected," a spokesman for the Merchant Organisation said.
Employment costs for shop staff rose by around 5.8 percent per hour.
